body: Valkyria Chronicles II is Sega's PSP tactical role-playing game, first released in Japan on 21 January 2010. Two years after the earlier war, military-academy cadets become involved in a struggle against rebels pursuing an ethnic-cleansing campaign. The school gives the story a continuing social setting between operations, while the battlefield retains the series' mixture of planning and direct control. The player selects a unit, then moves and acts from close behind it within the limits available. A tactical decision becomes something performed through the soldier rather than resolved entirely from a distant map.

Command-level decisions determine which unit acts and how the available effort is distributed. Once selected, a soldier crosses the field under the player's control, making cover, distance and enemy fire practical concerns. Different classes provide different answers to an objective, encouraging the player to develop and use more than one kind of unit. The handheld format divides operations into compact areas, while the larger campaign supplies continuing progression. The player moves between thinking about the whole group and handling the immediate danger faced by the one character currently carrying out the plan.

Takeshi Ozawa directed the sequel, with Hitoshi Sakimoto returning to compose the music. The PSP release offered a more portable version of the series' unusual combat while building a new cast around the academy. North American and European editions followed later in 2010, and reviews were generally favourable. Its setting changes the interval between missions: classmates and their development become part of the campaign's structure. The result is a distinct continuation, linking a war being fought outside the school to the young people learning how to take part in it.
